newsitem.title: USA: Indian gaming revenues soar, study shows.
newsitem.headline: Indian gaming revenues soar, study shows.

text.p: Revenues from gaming run by native American Indian tribes soared to more than $4.5 billion in 1995, up 3,500 percent from less than $15 million in 1985, a congressional report showed Sunday.

Releasing the report, the Republican chairman of the tax-writing House Ways and Means Committee, Representative Bill Archer of Texas, said part of the success of Indian gaming can be attributed to "unfair tax advantages."
The General Accounting Office, the audit arm of Congress, reported that Indian gaming revenues totalled at least 10 percent of the U.S. gaming market in 1995.

As of December 31, 1996, 184 tribes were operating 281 gaming facilities, the report said. It said the largest such facilities, including casino games and slots, generated higher operating income as a percentage of total revenues than the largest Nevada and Atlantic City, N.J., casinos.
